classificationReport.criteria: C4 (High=direct asset theft/loss via valid path; Medium=protocol function/availability impact or value leak w/ stated assumptions+external requirements; Low=state-handling/spec-deviation/centralization; QA=doc/style)
classificationReport.lawContext: All 7 candidates were pre-adjudicated by dedup+sanitizer to have NO unprivileged theft path. Remaining vectors are Law-3 non-obvious owner/operator footguns (in scope, classified by unlocked impact) and Law-2 faithfulness residuals (routed to spec-conformance F-XX). None escalate to High/Medium: no direct asset theft/loss, no permissionless availability brick, and every value-motion path is value-conserving and owner-recoverable.
classificationReport.labelScheme: Run-19 renumbers L-/Q- from 01. DEDUP-19-004 is NOT given a new run-19 label — it consolidates into the OPEN run-18 ledger L-01 (fp 966e7176...). The other six take fresh run-19 labels L-01..L-04 / Q-01..Q-02.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01 (run-18, CONSOLIDATE — augment existing OPEN entry; no new run-19 label)

consolidation.decision: CONSOLIDATE into run-18 L-01 (fp 966e717669f973ff2fff36e5ed65fb98e287700bbdfc5ab4e8047407d8b5b8b4, status=open) as a second strand — do NOT mint a separate run-19 sibling Low.
consolidation.sameRootCause: The migrator's immutable stakedId carries no parity assertion against the staker's owner-mutable live stakedId(); claimTimedOut (L254) and rescueERC1155 (L283-284) both key off the migrator's frozen copy.
consolidation.strandDifference: Run-18 L-01 = DEPLOY-TIME mis-wire strand (constructor never cross-checks stakedId/stakedToken -> strandable parked principal). DEDUP-19-004 = DYNAMIC POST-DEPLOY strand (a legitimate setStakedId reissue, allowed while totalStaked==0, drifts the two apart AFTER a correct deploy -> kills the permissionless claimTimedOut hatch AND voids the rescueERC1155 totalParked floor).
consolidation.reAuditTrap: IMPORTANT: L-01's currently-recommended remediation (a CONSTRUCTOR cross-check) does NOT close DEDUP-19-004. A constructor-only assert passes at deploy and then drifts on a later setStakedId. Consolidation therefore REQUIRES upgrading L-01's remediation from a one-time constructor assert to a LIVE/DYNAMIC parity read (assert migrator.stakedId == staker.stakedId() at the point of use in claimTimedOut/rescueERC1155/migrateIn, or read staker.stakedId() directly). Record this incomplete-fix risk on the ledger note so a constructor-only patch is not auto-flipped to fixed.
consolidation.law1Visibility: Consolidation is NOT a drop: the dynamic-drift consequences are folded into L-01's writeup as expanded impact + augmented remediation, and the incomplete-fix trap is recorded on the ledger entry. Recall preserved.

classification.assetImpact: No direct/permissionless theft. Two owner/operator-config hazards: (1) AVAILABILITY — a stakedId reissue during the in-place migration window makes the permissionless claimTimedOut self-rescue transfer the wrong (frozen) id, reverting the parked user's escape hatch; (2) SAFETY-RAIL LOSS — rescueERC1155's totalParked floor (designed to protect parked principal 'even against the owner', L276-286) is computed on balanceOf(this, migrator.stakedId); if that frozen id no longer matches the physically-parked tokens, the floor check no longer guards the real parked balance, so a subsequent onlyOwner rescueERC1155 could sweep parked principal the floor was meant to fence off.
attackPath: 1. Correct deploy: migrator.stakedId == staker.stakedId() (deploy strand of L-01 not triggered).
2. Operator runs initiateMigration + migrateOut: users' ERC1155 (current id) parked in migrator custody; totalParked set.
3. During the reset/rewire window (totalStaked==0) the owner performs the DOCUMENTED NFT-reissue: staker.setStakedId(newId). This is a spec-blessed reconfig (Feature Spec item 1/6), not misuse.
4. Drift is now live: staker.stakedId()==newId but migrator.stakedId==oldId (frozen at construction).

5a. Escape-hatch break: a parked user calls claimTimedOut after migrationTimeout -> transfers migrator.stakedId (old id). If the parked custody now holds/expects a different id post-reissue, the transfer reverts (or returns the wrong id) -> permissionless self-rescue unavailable.

5b. Floor void: rescueERC1155 measures the floor against migrator.stakedId's balance; the totalParked fence no longer aligns with the actually-parked tokens, so the 'even against the owner' guarantee is defeated -> an owner rescue can reach parked principal.
classification.likelihood: low — requires the operator to interleave a setStakedId reissue with an IN-FLIGHT in-place migration (parked stake outstanding). Both are legitimate individually; the hazard is the non-obvious ordering coupling. No attacker; no permissionless trigger.
classification.assumptions: Parked stake is outstanding (post-migrateOut, pre-migrateIn) at the moment setStakedId is called; the reissued id differs from the frozen migrator id.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner/operator action only (setStakedId is onlyOwner + totalStaked==0-gated; rescueERC1155 is onlyOwner). No external/attacker requirement. Fully avoidable with correct sequencing and fully recoverable (migrateIn still returns funds; owner does not sweep).
classification.law3Test: A competent, non-malicious operator WOULD be surprised that reissuing the NFT id mid-migration silently disarms both the timeout hatch and the anti-owner rescue floor -> non-obvious footgun -> in scope (not a malicious-owner vector).

classifiedFindings.justification: Same contract, same 'immutable stakedId lacks live-parity assertion' root as OPEN run-18 L-01 — a dynamic-drift strand of one bug, not a second bug. Ceiling Low: no unprivileged theft (rescue is onlyOwner), availability harm is owner-recoverable via migrateIn, and the trigger is an owner-sequencing footgun. Consolidate + augment L-01's remediation to a live parity read (constructor-only fix is an incomplete-fix / re-audit trap).

classifiedFindings.label: Q-01

classification.assetImpact: None. NFTStakerMigrator stores an immutable stakedId that migrate() never references and never asserts equal across the old/new stakers. A cross-staker stakedId mismatch surfaces only as a hard revert with clean atomic rollback (no partial state, no fund loss). The dead immutable is misleading — it implies a parity guarantee the code does not enforce.
attackPath: 1. Deploy NFTStakerMigrator with a stakedId that does not match one of the wired stakers (or the stakers disagree).
2. Call migrate(): the ERC1155 move reverts on the id mismatch; the whole call rolls back atomically.
3. No funds move; operator observes a failed migration and re-deploys with correct wiring.
classification.likelihood: n/a — no exploit path; worst case is a self-evident revert at migration time.
classification.law3Test: Distinct from DEDUP-19-004: here the failure mode is a clean DoS-revert with rollback (no silent floor-void, no stranded principal), so it is QA hardening, not an operational hazard that unlocks impact.

classifiedFindings.justification: Pure code-hygiene / dead-immutable + misleading-documentation issue on a distinct contract (NFTStakerMigrator, no prior ledger entry). Fail-loud, value-conserving, no fund risk -> QA. Recommend either wiring the immutable into a real cross-staker parity assert in migrate() or removing it.

classifiedFindings.label: L-01
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRouting: Route to spec-conformance report as F-19-01 (Law 2). NOT a regression of ledger M-01 (fp b58b172e, fixed @321d0a9) — sanitizer regressionRuledOut=true.

classification.assetImpact: None (value-conserving, solvency-safe). depositFor still carries an UNCONDITIONAL tail _recomputeSchedule that restarts windowEnd = now + windowSeconds on every call — the same window-restart CLASS story-020 removed from the permissionless stake/unstake paths. Because depositFor is onlyMigrator (trusted, non-permissionless) and cannot be repeatably invoked by an attacker to grief the window, the residual is a faithfulness/operational deviation, not the reintroduced M-01 exploit. The NatSpec claim of 'parity with stake' is now stale/false (stake no longer recomputes post-story-020).
attackPath: 1. (No attacker path.) Owner-orchestrated migrateIn -> staker.depositFor(user, amt) runs the unconditional tail recompute.

2. Each re-injection restarts the depletion window, deferring the horizon; because inflow through the migrator is a genuine re-seed this is value-conserving, but the behaviour diverges from the post-story-020 stake() semantics the NatSpec still claims parity with.
classification.likelihood: low — trusted onlyMigrator surface; no permissionless or repeatable griefing trigger.
classification.assumptions: depositFor is only reachable via the InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator (onlyMigrator).
classification.regressionNote: Explicitly NOT M-01 regression: different function surface (depositFor vs stake/unstake tail), trusted caller, value-conserving. The story-020 M-01 guard HELD on the permissionless paths.

classifiedFindings.justification: Spec-deviation / stale-NatSpec residual on a trusted path with no asset, availability, or unprivileged-griefing impact -> Low. Carries faithfulness:true and routes to spec-conformance as F-19-01 (Law 2 — surfaced, not buried in QA noise), at its honest Low severity (no value/availability impact to bump it per Law 1). Recommend gating the depositFor tail recompute on inflow>0 to mirror the story-020 stake/unstake fix, and correcting the 'parity with stake' NatSpec.

classifiedFindings.label: Q-02
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRouting: Route to spec-conformance report as F-19-02 (Law 2) even though impact is doc-only — a story-020 behavioural-doc deviation is reported visibly to the owner, never dropped into gas-report noise.

classification.assetImpact: None (documentation-only). Post-story-020 the no-hook branch of _syncBudget settles accrual only (pure _updatePool, no _recomputeSchedule), but the NatSpec still claims it 'behaves like a pure recompute'. The docstring was made stale BY the story-020 fix. No functional impact: every config setter recomputes directly, so no code path relies on the stale claim.
attackPath: 1. (No exploit.) A reader/maintainer trusts the stale NatSpec and assumes the no-hook branch recomputes the schedule.
2. Risk is future-maintenance confusion only; runtime behaviour is correct and unchanged.

classifiedFindings.justification: Pure doc-drift introduced by the story-020 fix, zero functional impact -> QA. Tagged faithfulness:true and routed to spec-conformance as F-19-02 (Law 2 obliges surfacing story-behaviour doc deviations to the owner) rather than folding it silently into the gas/style bundle. Recommend updating the _syncBudget no-hook-branch NatSpec to 'settles accrual only; no recompute'.

classifiedFindings.label: L-02
classifiedFindings.faithfulnessRouting: Route to spec-conformance report as F-19-03 (Law 2). It is an INTENDED consequence of story-020 but a NON-OBVIOUS operational footgun (Law 3) — reported as an operational hazard with safe-config guidance, not suppressed as trusted-owner noise.

classification.assetImpact: None (value never lost). finalizeAndReset revives a drained Migrating pool to Active but does NOT recompute the schedule. Post-story-020 stake() no longer auto-rearms the window, so a revive-then-organic-stake sequence (no depositFor re-seed via the migrator) emits ZERO rewards until the owner explicitly re-arms via setDepletionWindow / topUp. Emissions PAUSE, they are not destroyed; principal is untouched.
attackPath: 1. Pool is drained/Migrating; owner calls finalizeAndReset -> Active (no schedule recompute).
2. A new user stakes organically (plain stake(), not the migrator's depositFor path which self-heals via its own recompute per DEDUP-19-006).
3. Because story-020 removed the stake tail recompute, windowEnd stays dormant -> the staker accrues nothing until the owner calls setDepletionWindow/topUp to re-arm.
4. Owner re-arms -> emissions resume. No value lost, only a silent emission gap until re-arm.
classification.likelihood: low — requires the specific revive-via-finalizeAndReset THEN organic-stake (not migrator-re-injection) ordering, and the owner not re-arming first.
classification.assumptions: Pool revived via finalizeAndReset with no depositFor re-seed; an organic stake precedes owner re-arm.
classification.externalRequirements: Owner operational sequencing only. No attacker. Fully owner-recoverable (setDepletionWindow/topUp).
classification.law3Test: A competent, non-malicious owner WOULD be surprised that reviving the pool and letting users stake yields zero emissions until a separate re-arm — the InPlace migrator path self-heals but the organic path does not. Non-obvious asymmetric consequence -> footgun -> in scope.

classifiedFindings.justification: Intended story-020 consequence surfaced as a non-obvious operational footgun (Law 3): emissions silently dormant after an organic revive until owner re-arm. Value-conserving and owner-recoverable, no attacker, no availability brick of principal -> Low. faithfulness:true, routed to spec-conformance as F-19-03. Recommend finalizeAndReset re-arm the window (or emit an explicit NEEDS-REARM signal / doc the required setDepletionWindow follow-up).

classifiedFindings.label: L-03

classification.assetImpact: None demonstrated in scope. In unstake (both NFTStaker and the NFTStakerPriceScaled copy) the outbound ERC1155 safeTransferFrom (onERC1155Received on a caller-chosen recipient) executes BEFORE the tail _recomputeSchedule, so during the receive callback totalStaked is already decremented while rewardRate/windowEnd still reflect the OLD pool. Value-reporting views (currentRewardRate/runwaySeconds/totalNFTValue) return a transiently inconsistent snapshot mid-callback. STATE-CHANGING reentry is blocked by the contract-wide nonReentrant. Impact requires an external oracle-style consumer that prices collateral off these views inside the callback — NONE known in scope.
attackPath: 1. Attacker unstakes to an attacker-controlled ERC1155 receiver.
2. Inside onERC1155Received, totalStaked is decremented but rewardRate/windowEnd not yet recomputed -> views read an inconsistent (stale-rate vs new-supply) snapshot.

3. A hypothetical downstream integrator that reads currentRewardRate/runwaySeconds/totalNFTValue during the callback and prices something off it could be misled. No such in-scope consumer exists; nonReentrant blocks any state-changing reentry back into the staker.
4. (No realized loss without an external victim contract.)
classification.likelihood: implausible (in current scope) — no known on-chain oracle/integrator consumes these views mid-callback; the only reachable effect is a read-only transient inconsistency.
classification.assumptions: A future/external contract reads the staker's value views atomically during another party's unstake callback and trusts them for pricing.
classification.externalRequirements: An out-of-scope downstream integrator that treats these views as an atomic oracle. Absent that, no impact.
classification.law1Note: Kept-not-dropped per Law 1 (victim is a plausible-future downstream integrator, not a current in-scope party). Ceiling Low; would only rise if an in-scope consumer of these views is later introduced.

classifiedFindings.justification: Read-only reentrancy view-inconsistency window with NO demonstrated in-scope victim and no state-changing reentry (nonReentrant holds). C4 treats consumer-less read-only reentrancy as Low/QA at best; retained at ceiling-Low (implausible-High) for visibility rather than QA because it is a genuine reentrancy-class exposure a future integrator could consume. Recommend moving the outbound transfer AFTER _recomputeSchedule (CEI) so views are consistent throughout the callback. Re-escalate only if an in-scope oracle/integrator of these views appears.

classifiedFindings.label: L-04

classification.assetImpact: None directly. DeployBatchNFTMinter.s.sol hardcodes DISPATCHER_INDEX (ASSUMED=4) and USDC as the nudge token, and the broadcast guards do NOT verify on-chain that the nudge token differs from the pinned dispatcher's primeToken() (that equality is only enforced at batchMint RUNTIME). A wrong index pins the batcher to the wrong dispatcher / payment asset at deploy; the misconfig is caught later by the runtime revert, not at deploy.
attackPath: 1. Operator runs the deploy script with the assumed DISPATCHER_INDEX=4 without confirming it matches the intended dispatcher on-chain.
2. Script broadcasts; no on-chain assert that nudgeToken != dispatcher.primeToken() (or that index 4 is the intended dispatcher).
3. A wrong index pins the BatchNFTMinter to the wrong dispatcher/payment asset.
4. Failure surfaces only at batchMint runtime (equality guard reverts) -> a redeploy/repoint is needed. No funds lost; operational rework only.
classification.likelihood: low — requires the operator to skip the NatSpec-documented manual confirm step; the runtime guard bounds the blast radius to a failed/mis-pinned deploy.
classification.assumptions: Operator does not perform the documented manual primeToken/index confirmation before broadcasting.
classification.externalRequirements: Operator action only; no attacker. Runtime-revert-mitigated and redeploy-recoverable.
classification.law3Test: A non-obvious deploy-config coupling (index<->dispatcher<->primeToken) that a competent operator could get wrong despite the NatSpec nudge -> footgun -> in scope, but low blast radius given the runtime guard.

classifiedFindings.justification: Deploy-script operator footgun (Law 3): a hardcoded assumed index / payment token with no on-chain deploy-time cross-check, mitigated by an existing NatSpec confirm instruction and a runtime equality revert. No asset loss, no attacker, redeploy-recoverable -> Low (QA-adjacent operational hazard). Recommend adding an on-chain deploy-time assert that nudgeToken != dispatcher.primeToken() and that the resolved dispatcher at DISPATCHER_INDEX is the intended one, failing the broadcast rather than deferring to runtime.

consolidationRecommendation.recommendation: CONSOLIDATE into run-18 L-01 as a second (dynamic-drift) strand — do NOT mint a separate run-19 sibling Low.
rationale: Same contract (src/InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol) and identical root cause: the immutable stakedId carries no live-parity assertion against the staker's owner-mutable stakedId().

Run-18 L-01 already frames the deploy-time mis-wire strand; DEDUP-19-004 develops the distinct post-deploy setStakedId dynamic-drift CONSEQUENCES (killed permissionless claimTimedOut hatch + voided rescueERC1155 totalParked floor). One bug, two strands; two Low labels for one missing assertion on one contract is report-noise.

CRITICAL augmentation condition (why this is not a silent merge): L-01's current remediation is a CONSTRUCTOR cross-check, which does NOT close the dynamic strand — a later setStakedId re-opens it. Consolidation must UPGRADE L-01's remediation to a LIVE/dynamic parity check (read staker.stakedId() at point-of-use in claimTimedOut/rescueERC1155/migrateIn) and record the incomplete-fix / re-audit trap on the ledger note so a constructor-only patch is not auto-flipped to fixed.
